model.name: Invoice / Commercial Document
model.purpose: Govern the commercial invoice and closely related billing documents as a payment claim, tax evidence object and, where applicable, a customs valuation document, without absorbing generic recordkeeping, payment execution or fulfilment semantics.
model.scope_statement: The model covers seller-initiated invoices, credit notes, debit notes processed as billing documents, self-billed invoices and credit notes, corrected and prepayment invoices, proforma invoices that do not claim payment, freight invoices as a billing subtype, and customs commercial invoices used to declare imported merchandise. It includes identity and type, parties and roles, line-level billed supply, allowances and charges, delivery and period, commercial references, VAT or other invoice tax breakdown, currencies and legal monetary totals, payment instructions, billing process states, and syntax-neutral compliance bindings to UBL, EN 16931 and UN/CEFACT CII.
in_scope: Credit notes and debit notes processed as billing documents
Self-billed invoices and self-billed credit notes
Proforma invoices that do not claim payment
Freight invoices as a billing subtype
Customs commercial invoices used to declare imported merchandise
Parties and roles: seller, buyer, payee, tax representative and delivery party
Line-level billed supply with items, quantities and prices
Document-level and line-level allowances and charges
Commercial references to orders, contracts, despatch, receipt and preceding invoices
VAT or other invoice tax breakdown
Payment instructions: means, terms, due date and payee
Syntax-neutral compliance bindings to UBL, EN 16931 and UN/CEFACT CII
out_of_scope: Generic document recordkeeping: version chains, renditions, digital signatures as preservation objects, chain of custody, retention schedules, legal holds and certified copies belong to N1 Document & Record.
Payment execution, remittance advice, cash application and settlement confirmation belong to WM-ECO-009.
Physical fulfilment, despatch advice and receipt advice as operational events belong to WM-ECO-024; this model stores only references to them.
Purchase orders, quotations, catalogues, contracts and tenders are referenced, not owned.
Customs declarations (entry, export, transit) are sibling trade documents; only the commercial invoice contents required for entry are in scope.
Tax returns, SAF-T, VAT ledgers and other tax-reporting documents are out of scope; UBL explicitly does not provide tax-reporting documents.
UBL Statement (statement of account), Reminder, Remittance Advice and Utility Statement are adjacent billing documents, not this core invoice object.
National clearance envelopes, Peppol transport receipts and access-point routing are interchange projections, not invoice semantics.

boundary_notes.distinction: N1 may govern an issued invoice as a record; WM-ECO-008 is the commercial and fiscal claim object and does not duplicate recordkeeping semantics.
WM-ECO-009 settles the payable amount; the invoice carries only payment instructions, prepaid amount and typed settlement links.
WM-ECO-024 supplies despatch and receipt evidence referenced by the invoice; the invoice stores typed references only.
Party legal entities, identifier schemes and calendars are referenced and snapshotted on the invoice, not duplicated as master data here.
These specifications are alignments that constrain semantics, cardinalities, codes and calculations; they are not the identity of the model.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Syntax and storage projections (XML, JSON, PDF, Peppol, MCP, MongoDB)
boundary_notes.distinction: These are projections of the invoice; none of them define invoice semantics.

sources.title: Universal Business Language Version 2.4
sources.relevance: Published by the OASIS Universal Business Language TC; defines the Invoice, CreditNote, DebitNote, SelfBilledInvoice, SelfBilledCreditNote and FreightInvoice document families, the Invoice as a request for payment from the Supplier Accounting Party to the Customer Accounting Party, InvoiceLine and Item structures, and the exclusion of tax-reporting documents.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0
sources.relevance: Published by the OpenPeppol Post-Award Coordinating Community; supplies the CIUS of EN 16931:2017, party roles (Customer/Supplier, Creditor/Debtor), billing profiles P1-P9, credit and correction processes, calculation rules including BR-CO-16, and payment means scope.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 UBL Invoice syntax
sources.relevance: Binds the semantic model to UBL Invoice elements: CustomizationID and ProfileID defaults, cbc:ID without scheme attribute, buyer reference versus purchase order reference, allowances and charges, InvoicePeriod, tax point date, LegalMonetaryTotal and amount formatting rules.

sources.title: EN 16931 compliance
sources.version_or_date: Page updated 5 March 2026; standard EN 16931-1 semantic CORE and CIUS rules
sources.relevance: European Commission Digital Building Blocks / eInvoicing page defining compliance at document, implementation and specification level, the CORE model, and the rule that a CIUS must be a subset of CORE and must not break CORE rules.

sources.title: Council Directive 2006/112/EC Article 226 - Content of invoices
sources.version_or_date: Directive of 28 November 2006; Article 226 content of invoices
sources.relevance: Official text of the VAT Directive as published on legislation.gov.uk; sets the mandatory invoice content model: sequential number based on one or more series, party names, addresses and VAT identification numbers, supply date, quantity and nature of supply, unit price exclusive of VAT, discounts, taxable amount per rate, VAT rate and amount, exemption or reverse-charge references, and the 'Self-billing' and 'Cash accounting' mentions.

sources.title: 19 CFR 141.86 Contents of invoices and general requirements
sources.version_or_date: Current 19 CFR 141.86 (origin T.D. 73-175; last cited amendment CBP Dec. 09-47)
sources.relevance: Legal Information Institute reproduction of the U.S. Customs and Border Protection regulation prescribing commercial invoice contents for import entry: port of entry; time, place and parties to the sale or shipment; merchandise description, marks and package numbers; quantities; purchase price or alternative value; kind of currency; itemized charges; rebates and bounties; country of origin; assists; English-language requirement; packing list; and the named responsible exporter employee.

sources.title: UN/CEFACT Cross Industry Invoice (CII) and Cross Industry Invoicing Process BRS
sources.version_or_date: CII maximum dataset; BRS Cross Industry Invoice v2.00.05; Executive Guide on eInvoicing 2023
sources.relevance: UNECE UN/CEFACT entry point describing CII as a maximum dataset covering commercial, transport, customs, fiscal and banking uses, and the acknowledged CII syntax binding for EN 16931.

sources.title: BRS Cross Industry Invoice v2.0.5
sources.version_or_date: Version 2.00.05, TBG approval 12 November 2008; PDF still published by UNECE
sources.relevance: UN/CEFACT TBG1 business requirements specification for the cross industry invoicing process, including supplier-initiated invoicing, self-billing with supplier reconciliation and dispute notice, self-billing credit notes, and consolidated, consignment and factored invoice variants; source of UNTDID 1001 document type usage.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: Establish what the commercial document is, which identifier is master, which functional type it has, and which legal class (tax invoice, payment claim, proforma, customs commercial invoice) it occupies.
bundles.rationale: Identity and legal class decide which content rules apply: Article 226 sequential numbering, the declared CORE or CIUS specification and business process, and the UNCL 1001 type code that separates a payment claim from a proforma, credit note or customs commercial invoice.

layers.name: Document identity
layers.description: How the invoice is identified inside the seller numbering series, and which specification and business process the instance declares to its receiver.

findings.name: Invoice identifier and numbering series
findings.description: A commercial invoice is identified first by a sequential number, based on one or more series, that uniquely identifies the invoice within the seller's business context, time-frame, operating systems and records. In EN 16931/Peppol this is BT-1 / UBL Invoice/cbc:ID, with no identification scheme attribute. A Dimension UUID is additional, not a substitute for the issuer number. A date is not an identifier.

questions.text: What sequential invoice number uniquely identifies this invoice inside the seller's chosen series and accounting system?
Which issuing accounting or e-invoicing master system is authoritative for assigning and guaranteeing uniqueness of the invoice number?
If a Dimension UUID or ULID is assigned, how is it bound to the seller invoice number without replacing Article 226 sequential identification?

data_elements.name: invoiceNumber
data_elements.description: Sequential number, based on one or more series, that uniquely identifies the invoice in the seller's business context (EN 16931 BT-1, UBL Invoice/cbc:ID, VAT Directive Article 226(2)).

data_elements.name: numberingSeriesId
data_elements.description: Identifier of the seller numbering series from which the invoice number was drawn.

data_elements.name: issuerAccountingSystemId
data_elements.description: Identifier of the issuing accounting or e-invoicing system that assigns the number and guarantees its uniqueness.

data_elements.name: dimensionUuid
data_elements.description: UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension in addition to, and not as a substitute for, the issuer invoice number.

data_elements.name: copyIndicator
data_elements.description: Indicator distinguishing a copy from the originally issued invoice instance.

data_elements.name: ublUuid
data_elements.description: UBL UUID carried alongside the seller invoice number in the UBL syntax projection.

artifacts.name: Invoice header identity block
artifacts.description: Issued invoice identity fragment containing the seller sequential number, series, issuing system and any Dimension UUID, independent of file encoding.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the seller sequential invoice number in its numbering series (EN 16931 BT-1 / UBL cbc:ID); any Dimension UUID is bound as a secondary identifier.

findings.name: Specification, profile and business process
findings.description: Interoperable electronic invoices declare the specification they conform to and the business process they belong to. Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 requires CustomizationID (default urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:3.0) and ProfileID (default urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:01:1.0) so a receiver can interpret cardinalities and rules. These URNs identify a CIUS/process, not the invoice instance.

questions.text: Which CORE invoice specification or CIUS does this instance claim to satisfy?
In which billing business process must the buyer process this invoice?
If a CIUS is used, which CORE optional elements were restricted out, and can a CORE-only receiver still process the instance?

data_elements.name: customizationId
data_elements.description: Specification identifier declaring the CORE specification or CIUS the instance conforms to; Peppol default urn:cen.eu:en16931:2017#compliant#urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:3.0.

data_elements.name: profileId
data_elements.description: Business process identifier telling the receiver which billing process applies; Peppol default urn:fdc:peppol.eu:2017:poacc:billing:01:1.0.

data_elements.name: ciusIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the CIUS narrowing CORE for this instance, where a CIUS rather than plain CORE is claimed.

data_elements.name: businessProcessType
data_elements.description: Billing business process the invoice belongs to, as interpreted from the profile identifier.

data_elements.name: syntaxBinding
data_elements.description: Syntax in which the declared semantic model is carried for this instance (UBL Invoice, UBL CreditNote or UN/CEFACT CII).

artifacts.name: CIUS and profile declaration
artifacts.description: Machine-readable declaration of CORE versus CIUS identifier and billing process profile used to validate the instance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the CustomizationID and ProfileID URNs carried on the parent invoice; the URNs identify a CIUS and process, not the instance.

layers.name: Document classification
layers.description: Which UNCL 1001 type code, UBL document type and legal class the instance carries, and whether it claims payment.

findings.name: Functional type and legal class
findings.description: UNTDID 1001 type codes distinguish commercial invoice (380), credit note (381), debit note (383), corrected invoice (384), prepayment invoice (386), tax invoice (388), self-billed invoice (389), factored invoice (393), consignment invoice (395) and proforma invoice (325). UBL Invoice is defined as a document used to request payment, submitted by the Supplier Accounting Party to the Customer Accounting Party. A proforma contains similar data but does not claim payment. A US customs commercial invoice is a valuation and entry document under 19 CFR 141.86 and is not the same legal act as an EU VAT invoice. Freight Invoice is a separate UBL document stating logistics charges.

questions.text: Which UNCL 1001 invoice or credit-note type code and UBL document type apply, and is the instance a payment claim, credit, proforma, tax invoice or customs commercial invoice?
If the receiver has no dedicated workflow for this type code, which synonym processing path applies (typically 380 for invoices and 381 for credit notes in Peppol BIS)?
Which N1 governed-record identity, if any, is attached to this commercial document without copying retention, signature or rendition fields into this model?

data_elements.name: invoiceTypeCode
data_elements.description: UNTDID/UNCL 1001 document type code such as 380 commercial invoice, 381 credit note, 383 debit note, 384 corrected invoice, 386 prepayment invoice, 388 tax invoice, 389 self-billed invoice, 393 factored invoice, 395 consignment invoice or 325 proforma invoice.

data_elements.name: legalClass
data_elements.description: Legal class the document occupies: tax invoice, payment claim, proforma, or customs valuation and entry document.

data_elements.name: claimsPaymentFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the document requests payment, as a UBL Invoice does, or carries similar data without claiming payment, as a proforma does.

data_elements.name: ublDocumentType
data_elements.description: UBL document family used for the instance: Invoice, CreditNote, DebitNote, SelfBilledInvoice, SelfBilledCreditNote or FreightInvoice.

data_elements.name: customsUseFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance is presented as a commercial invoice for customs valuation and entry under 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: taxInvoiceFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance performs the legal act of a VAT/tax invoice as distinct from a customs commercial invoice.

artifacts.name: Invoice type code assignment
artifacts.description: Record of UNCL 1001 code, UBL document type, legal class and whether the document claims payment or serves customs/proforma purposes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier together with the assigned UNCL 1001 type code and UBL document type.

bundles.name: Parties and authority
bundles.description: Identify seller, buyer and optional payee, tax representative and delivery parties, with legal names, addresses, VAT identifiers and electronic endpoints, including the inverted issuer in self-billing.
bundles.rationale: Article 226 requires full names, addresses and VAT identification numbers of the parties, Peppol routing depends on ISO 6523 ICD and EAS identifiers, and self-billing inverts the issuer role without moving the tax identity of the supply.

layers.name: Trading parties and roles
layers.description: Seller, buyer, payee, tax representative and delivery party roles as carried on the invoice, including the inverted issuer in self-billing.

findings.name: Seller, buyer and additional roles
findings.description: Peppol names Customer and Supplier as parties, and Creditor (invoice issuer, accounts receivable, seller) and Debtor (invoicee, accounts payable, buyer) as roles. UBL AccountingSupplierParty is mandatory on Invoice; AccountingCustomerParty is the buyer. PayeeParty is used when the payee differs from the seller. TaxRepresentativeParty carries the seller's tax representative. Article 226 requires full name and address of the taxable person and of the customer. In self-billing the Customer Accounting Party issues the invoice on behalf of the supplier.

questions.text: Who is the seller (taxable person supplying) and who is the buyer (customer), including legal name and address as they must appear on the invoice?
Is the payee different from the seller, and if so who is entitled to receive the payable amount?
In a self-billing arrangement, which party issues the invoice, and is the required 'Self-billing' mention present?
Which parties to the transaction, agents and tax authorities may read invoice content versus header-only metadata?

data_elements.name: sellerParty
data_elements.description: Supplier / creditor party (UBL AccountingSupplierParty), mandatory on the invoice, with the full legal name and address of the taxable person required by Article 226.

data_elements.name: buyerParty
data_elements.description: Customer / debtor party (UBL AccountingCustomerParty), with the full name and address of the customer required by Article 226.

data_elements.name: payeeParty
data_elements.description: UBL PayeeParty, used when the party entitled to receive payment differs from the seller.

data_elements.name: taxRepresentativeParty
data_elements.description: UBL TaxRepresentativeParty carrying the seller's tax representative.

data_elements.name: deliveryParty
data_elements.description: Party to whom the invoiced goods or services were delivered, as carried on the invoice.

data_elements.name: issuerRole
data_elements.description: Role actually issuing the invoice: supplier (creditor) in the normal case, customer in a self-billing arrangement.

data_elements.name: selfBillingFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the Customer Accounting Party issued the invoice on behalf of the supplier under a self-billing arrangement.

artifacts.name: Invoice party block
artifacts.description: Snapshot of seller, buyer, payee, tax representative and delivery party legal names, addresses and role assignments at issue time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus the party role (seller, buyer, payee, tax representative, delivery party); party master data is referenced, not mastered here.

layers.name: Tax and electronic identifiers
layers.description: VAT, legal-entity and electronic-address identifiers plus the buyer or purchase-order reference needed for tax content and routing.

findings.name: VAT, legal entity and electronic address identifiers
findings.description: Article 226 requires the supplier VAT identification number and, where the customer is liable or for intra-Community supplies, the customer VAT number. Peppol identifies parties with ISO 6523 ICD legal identifiers and Electronic Address Scheme (EAS) endpoints (BT-34/BT-49). An invoice must have a buyer reference or a purchase order reference. These identifiers reference party and identifier-scheme models; they do not duplicate organisation master data.

questions.text: Under which VAT identification numbers did the seller supply and, where required, did the buyer receive the supply?
Which electronic address scheme and endpoint identifiers should be used to route the invoice to seller and buyer?
What buyer reference or purchase-order reference is present to satisfy routing and the Peppol rule that at least one of BT-10 or BT-13 must exist?

data_elements.name: sellerVatId
data_elements.description: Supplier VAT identification number required on the invoice by Article 226(3).

data_elements.name: buyerVatId
data_elements.description: Customer VAT identification number, required where the customer is liable for the tax or for intra-Community supplies.

data_elements.name: sellerCompanyId
data_elements.description: Seller legal entity identifier expressed with an ISO 6523 ICD scheme.

data_elements.name: buyerCompanyId
data_elements.description: Buyer legal entity identifier expressed with an ISO 6523 ICD scheme.

data_elements.name: sellerEndpointId
data_elements.description: Seller electronic address endpoint (BT-34) used for interchange routing.

data_elements.name: buyerEndpointId
data_elements.description: Buyer electronic address endpoint (BT-49) used for interchange routing.

data_elements.name: buyerReference
data_elements.description: Buyer reference (BT-10); an invoice must carry either this or a purchase order reference.

data_elements.name: icdScheme
data_elements.description: ISO 6523 ICD scheme code qualifying a party legal identifier.

data_elements.name: easScheme
data_elements.description: Peppol Electronic Address Scheme code qualifying a party endpoint identifier.

artifacts.name: Party identifier set
artifacts.description: Governed set of VAT, company and electronic-address identifiers with scheme codes as carried on the invoice.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by scheme-qualified identifier values: VAT identification number, ISO 6523 ICD company identifier and Peppol EAS endpoint, each resolved against its issuing scheme.

bundles.name: Billed supply and references
bundles.description: Describe what is billed at line level, including items, quantities, prices, allowances and charges, delivery and invoicing period, and references to orders, contracts, despatch, receipt and preceding invoices.
bundles.rationale: Line-level supply, adjustments, delivery and period carry the content Article 226 and EN 16931 require, while typed references keep order, contract, despatch and receipt evidence in their own models yet verifiable from the invoice.

layers.name: Lines, items, allowances and charges
layers.description: Invoice lines with items, quantities and prices, and the allowances, charges, delivery data and invoicing period that adjust or qualify them.

findings.name: Invoice lines and priced items
findings.description: UBL InvoiceLine is a line structure containing an Item plus quantity, price and extension; Item names the generic item of sale, not a serialized instance. EN 16931/Peppol require at least one invoice line with invoiced quantity, unit of measure (UN/ECE Rec 20/21), item name/description, net line amount and unit price exclusive of VAT. Article 226 requires quantity and nature of goods or extent and nature of services, unit price exclusive of VAT, and discounts not included in the unit price.

questions.text: For each line, which seller, buyer or standard item identifiers and description identify the billed good or service?
What invoiced quantity, unit of measure and unit price exclusive of tax produce the line net amount?
Which order line, contract line or receipt line does this invoice line match for three-way verification?

data_elements.name: lineId
data_elements.description: Identifier of an invoice line within the invoice; at least one invoice line is required.

data_elements.name: itemName
data_elements.description: Name of the generic item of sale billed on the line, required by EN 16931/Peppol alongside the nature of goods or services required by Article 226.

data_elements.name: itemDescription
data_elements.description: Description of the billed good or service, covering the nature of goods or the extent and nature of services.

data_elements.name: sellersItemId
data_elements.description: Seller's identifier for the billed item.

data_elements.name: buyersItemId
data_elements.description: Buyer's identifier for the billed item.

data_elements.name: standardItemId
data_elements.description: Standard (scheme-issued) item identifier for the billed item.

data_elements.name: invoicedQuantity
data_elements.description: Quantity invoiced on the line, required by EN 16931/Peppol and by Article 226 as quantity of goods or extent of services.

data_elements.name: unitCode
data_elements.description: Unit of measure for the invoiced quantity, taken from UN/ECE Recommendation 20/21.

data_elements.name: unitPriceExclusiveTax
data_elements.description: Unit price exclusive of VAT, required by EN 16931/Peppol and Article 226; price amounts stay positive even when correcting by negative quantities.

data_elements.name: lineNetAmount
data_elements.description: Net amount of the invoice line, required by EN 16931/Peppol and used as the basis of document totals.

data_elements.name: lineTaxCategory
data_elements.description: VAT category applied to the invoice line, feeding the document tax breakdown.

artifacts.name: Invoice line list
artifacts.description: Ordered set of billed lines with item identity, quantity, unit, price and net amount used for matching and tax calculation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus the line identifier; items are generic items of sale, not serialized instances.

findings.name: Allowances, charges, period and delivery
findings.description: Document-level and line-level allowances and charges use a charge indicator, amount, VAT category and UNCL 5189/7161 reason codes. Delivery information states where and when invoiced goods or services were delivered. InvoicePeriod carries the invoicing or delivery period; if used, start and/or end date are required. Article 226 requires the supply date when it differs from the issue date. Location of delivery is invoice content, not a fulfilment event.

questions.text: Which document-level and line-level allowances and charges apply, with reason codes, amounts and tax categories?
On which date was the supply made or completed, and what invoicing or delivery period bounds the claim if it differs from the issue date?
Where were the invoiced goods or services delivered, including country of origin when required for customs or tax?

data_elements.name: allowanceChargeIndicator
data_elements.description: Indicator distinguishing an allowance from a charge at document or line level.

data_elements.name: allowanceChargeAmount
data_elements.description: Amount of the document-level or line-level allowance or charge.

data_elements.name: allowanceChargeReasonCode
data_elements.description: Reason code for the allowance or charge, taken from UNCL 5189 (allowances) or UNCL 7161 (charges).

data_elements.name: deliveryDate
data_elements.description: Date on which the invoiced goods or services were delivered; Article 226 requires the supply date when it differs from the issue date.

data_elements.name: deliveryLocation
data_elements.description: Place where the invoiced goods or services were delivered, carried as invoice content rather than as a fulfilment event.

data_elements.name: invoicePeriodStart
data_elements.description: Start date of the invoicing or delivery period; if InvoicePeriod is used, a start and/or end date is required.

data_elements.name: invoicePeriodEnd
data_elements.description: End date of the invoicing or delivery period; if InvoicePeriod is used, a start and/or end date is required.

data_elements.name: countryOfOrigin
data_elements.description: Country of origin of the billed goods, carried where required for customs or tax purposes.

artifacts.name: Adjustments and delivery block
artifacts.description: Document- and line-level allowances and charges plus delivery date, location and invoicing period as carried on the invoice.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus the allowance/charge position and reason code, or by the invoicing period bounds for period data.

layers.name: Commercial and preceding references
layers.description: Typed references from the invoice to orders, contracts, fulfilment documents, preceding invoices and supporting attachments.

findings.name: Order, contract, despatch, receipt and preceding invoice references
findings.description: An invoice should connect to an authentic commercial transaction: purchase order, sales order, contract, tender/lot, project, despatch advice and receipt advice. Preceding invoice references (BillingReference) identify invoices being credited or corrected. Additional supporting documents may be referenced by id, URL or embedded binary. Fulfilment documents remain WM-ECO-024 objects; this model stores typed references only.

questions.text: Which order, sales order, contract, tender or project identifiers authenticate the billed transaction?
Which WM-ECO-024 despatch advice and receipt advice instances does this invoice cite for delivery evidence?
Which preceding invoice identifiers and issue dates does a credit note or corrected invoice reverse or replace?

data_elements.name: orderReference
data_elements.description: Reference to the purchase order that authenticates the billed transaction; an invoice must carry either this or a buyer reference.

data_elements.name: salesOrderReference
data_elements.description: Reference to the seller's sales order for the billed transaction.

data_elements.name: contractReference
data_elements.description: Reference to the contract, tender or lot under which the supply was made.

data_elements.name: despatchAdviceReference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to the despatch advice held as a WM-ECO-024 fulfilment object.

data_elements.name: receiptAdviceReference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to the receipt advice held as a WM-ECO-024 fulfilment object.

data_elements.name: precedingInvoiceReference
data_elements.description: BillingReference identifying the invoice being credited or corrected by this document.

data_elements.name: precedingInvoiceIssueDate
data_elements.description: Issue date of the referenced preceding invoice.

data_elements.name: projectReference
data_elements.description: Reference to the project the billed transaction belongs to.

data_elements.name: supportingDocumentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to an additional supporting document by identifier, URL or embedded binary attachment.

artifacts.name: Commercial reference set
artifacts.description: Typed references from the invoice to orders, contracts, despatch/receipt documents, preceding invoices and supporting attachments.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus reference type and referenced document identifier; referenced documents stay in their own models.

bundles.name: Tax, currency and totals
bundles.description: Compute and record VAT or other invoice tax by category, dual reporting currency where required, and the legal monetary total chain that yields the amount due for payment.
bundles.rationale: The VAT regime must be determinable from the invoice itself, and Peppol calculation rules bind taxable amounts, document totals and the amount due for payment into one checkable chain.

layers.name: VAT regime and tax point
layers.description: VAT regime, category breakdown, exemption and reverse-charge references, and the date on which VAT becomes accountable.

findings.name: VAT breakdown, exemptions and tax point
findings.description: The invoice must allow determination of the VAT regime, calculation and description of tax per Directive 2006/112/EC. Required details include taxable amount per rate or exemption, VAT rate, VAT amount payable, and for exemption or customer-liability a reference to the Directive, national provision or reverse-charge indication. Peppol encodes categories with UNCL 5305 subset (S, Z, E, AE and others) and VATEX codes. TaxPointDate (BT-7) is required when VAT becomes accountable on a date different from issue date. Cash accounting requires the mention 'Cash accounting'. UBL tax structures are generic and not a tax-return document.

questions.text: On which date does VAT become accountable for seller and buyer if that date differs from the invoice issue date?
What taxable amounts, rates, category codes and tax amounts apply, including reverse charge or exemption references?
What invoice-held evidence allows a buyer or auditor to decide whether the invoice is correct from a VAT point of view?

data_elements.name: taxPointDate
data_elements.description: Date on which VAT becomes accountable (BT-7), required when it differs from the invoice issue date.

data_elements.name: taxCategoryCode
data_elements.description: VAT category code from the UNCL 5305 subset used by Peppol (S, Z, E, AE and others).

data_elements.name: taxRate
data_elements.description: VAT rate applied per category; for exempt or customer-liable categories a reference to the Directive, national provision or reverse-charge indication is carried instead.

data_elements.name: taxableAmount
data_elements.description: Taxable amount per rate or exemption, required by Article 226.

data_elements.name: taxAmount
data_elements.description: VAT amount payable per category, required by Article 226.

data_elements.name: exemptionReasonCode
data_elements.description: Reference to the Directive provision, national provision or other indication justifying an exemption.

data_elements.name: reverseChargeFlag
data_elements.description: Indication that the customer is liable for the tax under the reverse-charge mechanism.

data_elements.name: cashAccountingFlag
data_elements.description: Indication that cash accounting applies, requiring the mention 'Cash accounting' on the invoice.

data_elements.name: vatexCode
data_elements.description: VATEX code used by Peppol to encode the VAT exemption reason.

artifacts.name: Tax subtotal schedule
artifacts.description: Per-category tax breakdown with taxable amounts, rates, tax amounts, exemption or reverse-charge references and tax point date.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus VAT category code and rate; the schedule is invoice tax evidence, not a tax-return document.

layers.name: Currency, rounding and legal monetary totals
layers.description: Document currency, VAT accounting currency, rounding and the legal monetary total chain ending in the amount due for payment.

findings.name: Currency, totals and amount due for payment
findings.description: Only one invoice currency (ISO 4217) is used except for VAT accounting currency (BT-6) paired with invoice total VAT in accounting currency (BT-111). LegalMonetaryTotal carries line extension, allowance/charge totals, tax exclusive/inclusive amounts, prepaid amount, rounding and payable amount. Peppol BR-CO-16: Amount due for payment (BT-115) = Invoice total with VAT (BT-112) - Paid amount (BT-113) + Rounding amount (BT-114). Amounts are decimal with at most two fraction digits. Price amounts stay positive when correcting by negative quantities.

questions.text: Which ISO 4217 document currency applies, and is a separate VAT accounting currency and VAT amount in that currency required?
Do the stored totals satisfy BT-115 = BT-112 - BT-113 + BT-114 and the two-decimal amount rule?
What amount has already been paid or prepaid against this invoice, and what outstanding amount is requested?

data_elements.name: documentCurrencyCode
data_elements.description: ISO 4217 invoice currency; only one invoice currency is used per document.

data_elements.name: taxCurrencyCode
data_elements.description: VAT accounting currency (BT-6), used only where VAT must be reported in a currency other than the invoice currency.

data_elements.name: lineExtensionAmount
data_elements.description: Sum of invoice line net amounts carried in LegalMonetaryTotal.

data_elements.name: allowanceTotalAmount
data_elements.description: Sum of document-level allowances carried in LegalMonetaryTotal.

data_elements.name: chargeTotalAmount
data_elements.description: Sum of document-level charges carried in LegalMonetaryTotal.

data_elements.name: taxExclusiveAmount
data_elements.description: Invoice total without VAT carried in LegalMonetaryTotal.

data_elements.name: taxInclusiveAmount
data_elements.description: Invoice total with VAT (BT-112) carried in LegalMonetaryTotal.

data_elements.name: prepaidAmount
data_elements.description: Paid amount (BT-113) already settled against the invoice and subtracted from the amount due.

data_elements.name: payableRoundingAmount
data_elements.description: Rounding amount (BT-114) added when deriving the amount due for payment.

data_elements.name: payableAmount
data_elements.description: Amount due for payment (BT-115), equal to BT-112 - BT-113 + BT-114 under Peppol rule BR-CO-16, expressed with at most two fraction digits.

artifacts.name: Legal monetary total block
artifacts.description: Calculated document totals including tax exclusive/inclusive amounts, prepaid and rounding adjustments and the amount due for payment, with currencies.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier; exactly one legal monetary total block exists per invoice, in the single document currency.

bundles.name: Settlement claim
bundles.description: Record how the buyer is instructed to pay the claim, without executing or confirming payment, including means, terms, due date and factoring notes.
bundles.rationale: An invoice issued before payment is a request to pay, so payment means, terms, due date and payee are invoice content, while payment execution and confirmation stay in WM-ECO-009.

layers.name: Payment means, terms and payee
layers.description: Payment means, payee account, terms and due date carried on the invoice as instructions rather than as payment records.

findings.name: Payment means, due date and payee instructions
findings.description: An invoice issued before payment is a request to pay and commonly carries payment means (UNCL 4461), payee financial account, SEPA indicators and payment terms. If Amount due for payment is positive, either Payment due date (BT-9) or Payment terms (BT-20) shall be present. Credit transfer, direct debit and payment card are in scope of Peppol BIS; actual payment objects belong to WM-ECO-009. Factoring may be noted in invoice notes when the claim is assigned.

questions.text: By which date must payment be made, and which payment means and account should the debtor use?
Which WM-ECO-009 payment instances, if any, already settle part or all of this invoice's payable amount?
Has the invoice claim been assigned to a factor or other payee, and what notice must the buyer act on?

data_elements.name: paymentMeansCode
data_elements.description: UNCL 4461 payment means code; credit transfer, direct debit and payment card are in scope of Peppol BIS.

data_elements.name: payeeFinancialAccountId
data_elements.description: Financial account identifier to which the payable amount should be transferred.

data_elements.name: paymentDueDate
data_elements.description: Payment due date (BT-9); if the amount due for payment is positive, either this or payment terms shall be present.

data_elements.name: paymentTerms
data_elements.description: Payment terms (BT-20); if the amount due for payment is positive, either this or the payment due date shall be present.

data_elements.name: sepaIndicator
data_elements.description: Indicator that SEPA credit transfer or direct debit rules apply to the payment instruction.

data_elements.name: cardPaymentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the payment card used or to be used for settlement.

data_elements.name: factoringNote
data_elements.description: Invoice note recording that the claim has been assigned to a factor or other payee.

data_elements.name: amountDueForPayment
data_elements.description: Amount the debtor is requested to pay, carried as the invoice claim presented to a settlement process.

artifacts.name: Payment instruction block
artifacts.description: Invoice-held payment means, account, terms and due date used to initiate settlement in a payment model, not a payment record.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus payment means code and payee financial account; payment execution records are identified in WM-ECO-009.

bundles.name: Lifecycle, process and compliance
bundles.description: Govern issuance, buyer handling, credit and correction, self-billing, prepayment, validation against CORE/CIUS rules, and the distinct customs commercial-invoice content path.
bundles.rationale: Issued invoices are corrected by successor documents rather than mutation, Peppol profiles define the buyer handling paths, compliance is decided against CORE and CIUS rules, and the customs commercial invoice is a separate mandatory content profile.

layers.name: Billing process and corrections
layers.description: Issuance and buyer handling states, correction paths, and the special self-billing, prepayment, consolidated and consignment processes.

findings.name: Issuance, acceptance, credit and correction
findings.description: The invoicing process is issue and send from supplier to customer, then buyer handling: full approval and payment, complete rejection with a credit-note request, or partial dispute with credit note plus a new invoice. Peppol profiles P1-P9 cover order-based, contract-based, incidental, pre-payment, spot, advance, despatch-referenced, despatch-and-receipt-referenced, and credit/negative-amount cases. Crediting may use document type 381 (credit note) with positive line representation, or a 380 invoice with negative quantities and amounts; unit prices remain positive. UBL Credit Note is a supplier document specifying a reduced payment. Corrected invoice (384) carries revised information differing from an earlier submission. Issued invoices are not silently overwritten.

questions.text: What is the current billing status of this invoice (draft, issued, sent, accepted, rejected, disputed, credited, corrected, cancelled), and when did that state occur?
If the buyer rejected or disputed the invoice, is correction done by credit note 381, negative-amount invoice 380, or corrected invoice 384, and which preceding invoice is referenced?
Was this instance already issued, and if so which fields are frozen versus represented only on a successor credit or corrected document?
Who issued, sent, approved or disputed the invoice, and what is the chain from draft to the currently effective claim?

data_elements.name: billingStatus
data_elements.description: Current billing state of the invoice: draft, issued, sent, accepted, rejected, disputed, credited, corrected or cancelled.

data_elements.name: issuedAt
data_elements.description: Time at which the invoice was issued, recorded as an event time distinct from ingestion or observation time.

data_elements.name: sentAt
data_elements.description: Time at which the issued invoice was sent from supplier to customer.

data_elements.name: buyerDecision
data_elements.description: Buyer handling outcome: full approval and payment, complete rejection with a credit-note request, or partial dispute.

data_elements.name: creditNoteId
data_elements.description: Reference to the credit note (type 381) issued against this invoice.

data_elements.name: correctedInvoiceId
data_elements.description: Reference to the corrected invoice (type 384) carrying revised information for an earlier submission.

data_elements.name: correctionMethod
data_elements.description: Chosen correction process: credit note 381 with positive lines, negative-amount invoice 380, or corrected invoice 384.

data_elements.name: disputeReason
data_elements.description: Reason recorded when the buyer disputes or rejects the invoice in whole or in part.

data_elements.name: peppolProcessCode
data_elements.description: Peppol billing profile (P1-P9) governing the process this invoice is handled under.

artifacts.name: Billing lifecycle event record
artifacts.description: Event record of issue, send, approve, reject, dispute, credit or correction linked to the invoice instance, with event time distinct from ingestion time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the parent invoice identifier plus event type and event time, with observation or ingestion time recorded separately.

artifacts.name: Credit note or corrected invoice
artifacts.description: Credit note (UBL CreditNote / type 381) or corrected invoice (type 384) that adjusts a preceding invoice rather than mutating it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by its own sequential number in the issuer series together with the preceding invoice reference and issue date it adjusts.

findings.name: Self-billing, prepayment and special processes
findings.description: UN/CEFACT CII treats traditional supplier-initiated invoices and self-billing as first-class processes; the customer raises a self-billing invoice and the supplier reconciles it, raising a dispute notice on discrepancy, corrected by a self-billing credit note. UBL SelfBilledInvoice is created by the Customer Accounting Party. Article 226(10a) requires the mention 'Self-billing'. Prepayment invoices (386) collect amounts to be subtracted from a final invoice. CII also names consolidated, consignment and factored variants. These are rare relative to 380 but are not optional footnotes in a full model.

questions.text: Is this a self-billed invoice, which agreement authorises it, and has the supplier accepted or disputed it?
If this is a prepayment invoice, which final invoice will absorb the prepaid amount, or if this is a final invoice, which prepayments are deducted?
Is the invoice consolidated, consignment (non-sale), factored or freight-charge billing, and which process rules then apply?

data_elements.name: selfBillingFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the customer raised the invoice in the supplier's name, requiring the Article 226(10a) mention 'Self-billing'.

data_elements.name: selfBillingAgreementRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the agreement that authorises the customer to issue invoices on behalf of the supplier.

data_elements.name: prepaymentFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance is a prepayment invoice (type 386) collecting amounts to be subtracted from a final invoice.

data_elements.name: consolidatedFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance is a consolidated invoice variant named by UN/CEFACT CII.

data_elements.name: consignmentFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance is a consignment (non-sale) invoice variant, UNCL 1001 code 395.

data_elements.name: disputeNoticeId
data_elements.description: Reference to the dispute notice the supplier raises when reconciliation of a self-billing invoice finds a discrepancy.

artifacts.name: Self-billed invoice
artifacts.description: Invoice issued by the customer in the name of the supplier under a self-billing agreement, including the Self-billing mention.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the sequential number assigned by the issuing customer under the self-billing agreement, bound to the supplier party whose supply it documents.

layers.name: Compliance validation and customs commercial invoice
layers.description: Validation against CORE, CIUS and syntax schemas, and the separate customs commercial invoice content profile required for import entry.

findings.name: CORE, CIUS, syntax binding and validation
findings.description: EN 16931 defines compliance at document, implementation and specification levels. A document must contain mandatory information, structured as specified, with specified calculations and allowed codes. A compliant receiver must accept CORE or a permitted CIUS; a CIUS must be a subset of CORE and not break CORE rules. Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is a CIUS of EN 16931:2017 and binds the semantic model to UBL Invoice/CreditNote; CII syntax is also acknowledged. Validation stacks UBL schema, EN 16931 Schematron (BR-*, BR-CL-*, BR-CO-*) and Peppol rules. Alignment is not claimed as full conformance without a validation artefact. Directive 2014/55 obliges public entities to receive EN 16931 invoices but does not forbid other specifications.

questions.text: Which semantic model and syntax binding (UBL Invoice, UBL CreditNote, UN/CEFACT CII, or another) carry this instance?
Which fatal and warning rules fired, and is the instance CORE-compliant, CIUS-compliant, or non-compliant?
Is the receiver a public entity obliged to accept EN 16931 CORE/CIUS invoices, and may it still accept a narrower national CIUS only?

data_elements.name: semanticModelId
data_elements.description: Identifier of the semantic model the instance implements, typically the EN 16931 CORE model or a CIUS of it.

data_elements.name: syntaxBinding
data_elements.description: Syntax carrying the semantic model for validation: UBL Invoice, UBL CreditNote or UN/CEFACT CII.

data_elements.name: validationProfile
data_elements.description: Validation stack applied to the instance: syntax schema, EN 16931 Schematron and CIUS-specific rules.

data_elements.name: schematronResult
data_elements.description: Result of Schematron validation against CORE and the declared CIUS, listing passed and failed assertions.

data_elements.name: fatalRuleIds
data_elements.description: Identifiers of fatal rules that fired during validation (BR-*, BR-CL-*, BR-CO-* and Peppol rules).

data_elements.name: coreCompliantFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the instance satisfies EN 16931 CORE compliance at document level.

data_elements.name: ciusId
data_elements.description: Identifier of the CIUS the instance was validated against, where compliance is claimed against a CIUS rather than plain CORE.

artifacts.name: Invoice validation report
artifacts.description: Result of schema and Schematron validation against CORE and the declared CIUS, listing passed and fatal rules.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the validated invoice identifier plus the declared CustomizationID/ProfileID and the validation run time.

findings.name: Customs commercial invoice contents
findings.description: A US import commercial invoice must set forth port of entry; time, place and parties to the sale or shipment; detailed merchandise description with marks and package numbers; quantities; purchase price or alternative value; kind of currency; itemized charges (freight, insurance, commission, packing); rebates and bounties; country of origin; and assists not included in the invoice price. English language or translation is required; a packing list must state contents of each package; discounts must be detailed; a responsible exporter employee must be named. Merchandise sold in transit requires the original and resale invoices, or a pro forma substitute. This legal function is valuation for duties, not a VAT payment claim, and must not be collapsed into EN 16931 CORE.

questions.text: Which 19 CFR 141.86 content elements are present (port, parties, description, quantities, price or value, charges, origin, assists) and which are missing?
Was the merchandise sold in transit, and are both the original export invoice and the resale invoice (or a pro forma substitute) filed?
Is this instance serving as a tax/payment invoice, a customs valuation invoice, or both, and which content profile is therefore mandatory?
Which named exporter employee is responsible for knowledge of the customs transaction?

data_elements.name: portOfEntry
data_elements.description: Port of entry to which the merchandise is destined, required by 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: salePlace
data_elements.description: Place of the sale or shipment, required by 19 CFR 141.86 together with the time and parties.

data_elements.name: saleTime
data_elements.description: Time of the sale or shipment, required by 19 CFR 141.86 together with the place and parties.

data_elements.name: merchandiseDescription
data_elements.description: Detailed description of the merchandise, required by 19 CFR 141.86 in English or with a translation.

data_elements.name: packageMarks
data_elements.description: Marks and numbers of the packages in which the merchandise is packed, required by 19 CFR 141.86 alongside a packing list stating the contents of each package.

data_elements.name: quantity
data_elements.description: Quantities of the merchandise entered, required by 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: purchasePriceOrValue
data_elements.description: Purchase price of each item, or the alternative value where the merchandise was not sold, required by 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: currencyKind
data_elements.description: Kind of currency in which the invoice values are expressed, required by 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: itemizedCharges
data_elements.description: Itemized charges such as freight, insurance, commission and packing, required by 19 CFR 141.86 where they apply.

data_elements.name: rebatesDrawbacksBounties
data_elements.description: Rebates, drawbacks and bounties allowed on exportation, required by 19 CFR 141.86 where they apply.

data_elements.name: countryOfOrigin
data_elements.description: Country of origin of the merchandise, required by 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: assists
data_elements.description: Assists provided to the production of the merchandise that are not included in the invoice price, required by 19 CFR 141.86 where they exist.

data_elements.name: responsibleExporterEmployee
data_elements.description: Named employee of the exporter responsible for knowledge of the customs transaction, required by 19 CFR 141.86.

data_elements.name: inTransitResaleFlag
data_elements.description: Whether the merchandise was sold in transit, in which case the original and resale invoices, or a pro forma substitute, must be filed.

artifacts.name: Customs commercial invoice
artifacts.description: Commercial invoice prepared for customs entry with valuation, origin, assists, charges and package contents as required by 19 CFR 141.86, distinct from a tax e-invoice.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the seller invoice number together with the entry and port of entry context in which it is presented; in-transit sales are identified by the original plus resale invoice pair or a pro forma substitute.

functions.name: Issue commercial invoice
functions.description: Assign a sequential invoice number in the seller series, freeze issue date and type code, snapshot seller and buyer, compute tax and legal totals, and mark the instance issued and immutable.
outputs: issued invoice carrying a sequential invoice number
tax breakdown and legal monetary totals
preconditions: the seller numbering series and issuing accounting system are known
effects: the invoice number is consumed in the seller series
issue date and type code are frozen
seller and buyer are snapshotted on the invoice
the instance becomes issued and immutable

functions.name: Validate against CORE or CIUS
functions.description: Check mandatory content, code lists, amount calculations and declared CustomizationID/ProfileID against EN 16931 CORE, the relevant CIUS and the chosen syntax schema.
inputs: invoice instance in its declared syntax
outputs: validation report listing passed and fatal rules
preconditions: the instance declares a specification identifier and a business process identifier
effects: the validation report is retained with the issued instance for tax audit

functions.name: Calculate legal monetary totals
functions.description: Derive line nets, document-level allowances and charges, tax exclusive/inclusive totals and amount due for payment, including dual-currency VAT when required.
inputs: invoice lines with quantities and unit prices
document currency and any VAT accounting currency
outputs: tax exclusive and tax inclusive totals
invoice total VAT in the accounting currency when required
preconditions: at least one invoice line exists
effects: the legal monetary total block is populated
the amount-due formula BT-115 = BT-112 - BT-113 + BT-114 and the two-decimal rule are satisfied

functions.name: Issue credit note or corrected invoice
functions.description: Create a successor 381 credit note, 384 corrected invoice or negative-amount 380 invoice that references the preceding invoice without mutating the issued original.
inputs: preceding invoice reference and issue date
outputs: credit note (381), corrected invoice (384) or negative-amount invoice (380)
preconditions: a preceding invoice has already been issued
effects: the successor document references the preceding invoice
the issued original is not mutated or overwritten

functions.name: Issue self-billed invoice
functions.description: Allow the customer, under agreement, to issue an invoice in the supplier's name, including the Self-billing mention, and capture supplier acceptance or dispute.
outputs: supplier acceptance status or dispute notice
preconditions: a self-billing agreement authorises the customer to issue in the supplier's name
effects: the issuer role is inverted to the customer while the supply stays the supplier's
supplier reconciliation outcome is captured, including a self-billing credit note where needed

functions.name: Match invoice to order and fulfilment
functions.description: Resolve typed references to order, contract, despatch advice and receipt advice so the buyer can verify the authentic commercial transaction.
inputs: despatch advice and receipt advice references
preconditions: typed commercial references are present on the invoice
effects: the buyer can verify the authentic commercial transaction before approval or dispute

functions.name: Present payment claim
functions.description: Expose payable amount, due date or terms, payment means and payee so a payment process can settle the invoice without storing the payment here.
inputs: payment due date or payment terms
payment means and payee financial account
outputs: payment claim presentation for a settlement process
preconditions: the amount due for payment is positive
either a payment due date or payment terms is present
effects: settlement can be initiated in WM-ECO-009 without storing payment execution records on the invoice

functions.name: Present customs commercial invoice
functions.description: Assemble the commercial invoice contents required for import entry, including origin, assists, itemized charges and in-transit resale documents.
inputs: purchase price or alternative value and kind of currency
itemized charges, rebates, country of origin and assists
outputs: commercial invoice contents for import entry
original and resale invoices, or a pro forma substitute, for merchandise sold in transit
preconditions: merchandise is being entered and a commercial invoice or pro forma substitute is required
effects: valuation and entry contents required by 19 CFR 141.86 are presented to customs, separately from any VAT payment claim

composition.purpose: An issued invoice may be governed as a record with versions, renditions, signatures, custody, retention and holds in N1; those fields are not duplicated here, and child-of-N1 remains an open governance choice. Registry validation flags allow a child of N1, but recordkeeping semantics already recur in N1 and must not be reinvented on the invoice.

Invoice is settled by payments; prepaid amounts and payment instructions live on the invoice, payment execution lives on the payment. Known relation: financial lifecycle. Peppol treats the invoice as a claim for payment and separately describes payment initiation.

Fulfilment references invoices as billing evidence; invoices reference despatch and receipt documents for verification. Known relation: billing evidence, carried by Peppol profiles P7/P8 and UBL Despatch/Receipt document references.

UBL Invoice, CreditNote, DebitNote, SelfBilledInvoice, SelfBilledCreditNote and FreightInvoice are syntax-neutral business-object alignments, not owned encodings. Registry validation flags name UBL, and UBL 2.4 is the current OASIS Standard document family for invoicing.

EN 16931 CORE and permitted CIUS specifications constrain semantic content, cardinalities, codes and calculations for European e-invoices. Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is a CIUS of EN 16931:2017, and Directive 2014/55 requires public-entity receipt of EN 16931 invoices.

CII is a maximum dataset covering commercial, transport, customs, fiscal and banking uses; most operational invoices are subsets. UN/CEFACT supplies the global multi-sector invoice process, including self-billing and credit/debit variants, and an EN 16931 syntax binding.

Seller, buyer, payee, tax representative and responsible exporter employees are parties mastered elsewhere and snapshotted on the invoice. Invoice law requires names, addresses and tax identifiers of parties, not a second organisation register.

owner_package_requirements: The owning package must publish AGENTS.md carrying Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL for this model.
The owning package must carry the invoice specification, storage type, interface and process documents that those URLs resolve to.
The owning package must not duplicate N1 recordkeeping, WM-ECO-009 payment execution or WM-ECO-024 fulfilment semantics; it holds typed references to them instead.
The owning package must keep UBL, EN 16931 and UN/CEFACT CII as alignments and syntax bindings rather than as the identity of the model.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Namespace the model under its registry entry and the model identifier WM-ECO-008. Code lists and scheme values (UNCL 1001, UNCL 5305, UNCL 4461, UNCL 5189/7161, ISO 4217, ISO 6523 ICD, Peppol EAS, UN/ECE Rec 20/21) stay in their issuing namespaces and are referenced by scheme, and CustomizationID/ProfileID URNs remain CEN and Peppol namespace values that are declared here, not minted here.
registry_links: WM-ECO-024 Fulfilment (despatch and receipt evidence reference)

canonicalization_rules: Monetary amounts are decimal with at most two fraction digits, expressed in the single document currency, with VAT additionally expressed in the VAT accounting currency only where BT-6/BT-111 apply.
Legal date-only fields (issue date, due date, tax point, supply date) are ISO 8601 calendar dates; operational instants use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.
Coded values are canonicalised against their issuing code lists (UNCL 1001, UNCL 5305, UNCL 4461, UNCL 5189/7161, ISO 4217, ISO 6523 ICD, Peppol EAS, UN/ECE Rec 20/21 units).
Price amounts remain positive; corrections are expressed through negative quantities and amounts or through a credit note, not by negating unit prices.
patch_rules: Issued invoices are not patched in place; corrections create successor documents (381 credit note, 384 corrected invoice, or 380 invoice with negative quantities and amounts).
Only draft (unissued) invoices may be mutated.
After issue, the only permitted additions are status events, successor credit or correction links and payment-settlement references, none of which change frozen commercial content.
compatibility_rules: A CIUS must be a subset of CORE and must not break CORE rules; a compliant receiver must accept CORE or a permitted CIUS.
Declared CustomizationID and ProfileID must remain resolvable so receivers can interpret cardinalities and rules; changing them changes the compatibility contract.

Syntax bindings (UBL Invoice/CreditNote, UN/CEFACT CII) are projections of one semantic model; production bindings commonly still target UBL 2.1 and CII D16B while UBL 2.4 is the current OASIS Standard.

identity_priority: authoritative master-system identifier: seller sequential invoice number assigned in the issuing accounting system (UBL Invoice/ID, EN 16931 BT-1, VAT Directive Article 226(2))
governed global identifier/IRI when an interchange or tax authority assigns one (Peppol transmission id, national e-invoice folio or UUID)
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record business event time (issue, tax point, supply, due, status change) separately from observation or ingestion time when those differ. Instants use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z. Legal date-only fields such as IssueDate remain ISO 8601 calendar dates and are never used as identifiers.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named by the sequential number assigned within a declared numbering series, unique inside the issuer's business context, time-frame, operating systems and records; credit notes, corrected invoices and self-billed invoices take their own sequential number in the issuing party's series; dates are never used as serial names, and reuse of voided numbers follows the issuer's stated reuse policy.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: An issued invoice is immutable; integrity is the combination of a content digest of the issued instance and satisfaction of declared calculation and code-list rules (including BT-115 = BT-112 - BT-113 + BT-114). Corrections create successor documents.

policies: Issued invoices are not updated in place; use credit notes, corrected invoices or negative-amount invoices.
Invoice numbers must be unique within the seller series and uniqueness window; dates are not identifiers.
Access defaults to parties on the invoice, their authorised agents and competent tax or customs authorities; other access is exception-based and audited.
Retention, legal holds and destruction of the invoice-as-record are executed through N1 using tax and customs minimum-retention overlays, not by deleting the commercial claim silently.

read: Inspect invoice header, parties, lines, tax, totals and status for a permitted subject
List invoices by seller, buyer, period, type code or unpaid payable amount
Retrieve validation report and reference set for audit or three-way match
create: Issue a seller invoice with sequential number, tax breakdown and legal totals
Issue a credit note or corrected invoice referencing a preceding invoice
Issue a self-billed invoice under agreement
Record a customs commercial invoice presentation for entry
update: After issue, record status events (sent, accepted, rejected, disputed) without changing frozen commercial content
Attach successor credit or correction links and payment-settlement references
delete: Delete is not permitted for issued invoices
Drafts may be discarded before number assignment becomes legally used
Disposition of the record copy follows N1 retention, holds and destruction evidence

roles.name: Seller / invoice issuer / creditor
responsibilities: Issue, send and, where needed, credit or correct invoices
Remain responsible for VAT on supplier-initiated invoices

roles.name: Buyer / invoicee / debtor
responsibilities: Receive, verify and approve or dispute invoices
Pay the amount due using stated means, or issue self-billed invoices when authorised

roles.name: Payee
responsibilities: Receive payment when different from the seller, including under factoring assignment notices

roles.name: Tax representative
responsibilities: Appear on the invoice where the seller's tax representative is the person liable or identified under Article 226

roles.name: Validator / access-point operator
responsibilities: Apply CORE/CIUS Schematron and syntax validation
Not acquire ownership of the commercial claim

roles.name: Customs importer or broker
responsibilities: Present a commercial invoice meeting 19 CFR 141.86 (or analogous) contents for entry

access.default_rule: Deny by default; grant invoice content to seller, buyer, declared payee, tax representative, and competent tax or customs authority; grant metadata-only to authorised AP/validators.
exceptions: Legal hold or audit may extend read access to regulators and courts without granting update rights
Factoring assignment may redirect payee-visible payment instructions without exposing unrelated line detail beyond what the assignment requires
Public e-invoicing clearance systems may be given a mandated reporting projection that is not full evidentiary content
audit_requirements: Record who read or exported invoice content versus metadata, with observation time in RFC 3339
Record issue, send, validation, credit, correction and access-exception events with actor and event time
Retain validation reports with the issued instance for tax audit

coverage.claim: This model covers the defensible operating surface of invoices and closely related commercial billing documents as aligned to OASIS UBL 2.4, Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 / EN 16931 CORE-CIUS, EU VAT Directive Article 226, UN/CEFACT CII processes, and US 19 CFR 141.86 customs commercial invoices. It does not claim a single global invoice law or completeness for every national clearance regime.

checklist.notes: Seller sequential invoice number is the master-system identifier; Dimension UUID is tertiary; dates excluded as identifiers.
Draft/issued/sent/accepted/rejected/disputed/credited/corrected plus self-billing acceptance and CII dispute notice.
Order, contract, despatch, receipt, preceding invoice, project, payee and payment references; typed edges to N1, WM-ECO-009, WM-ECO-024.
Issue date, tax point, supply date, due date, invoice period; event time versus observation/ingestion time.
Issuer, preceding invoice chain, in-transit resale original versus resale invoice, factoring assignment notice.
Seller remains commercial owner of the claim; payee may differ; self-billing inverts issuer without transferring tax identity of the supply.

known_omissions: National continuous-transaction-control systems (Italy SdI, India GST IRN/QR, Brazil NF-e, Mexico CFDI UUID folio, France PDP, Peppol PINT) are not modelled as first-class profiles.
EN 16931-1:2026 ViDA semantic additions are reported in secondary sources; the 2026 CEN text was not retrieved as a freely readable primary, so ViDA fields are a gap.
Hybrid Factur-X/ZUGFeRD PDF/A-3 containers are projections, not fully specified here.
Invoice Response (Peppol T111) is an adjacent transaction, not expanded.
Islamic finance, GCC e-invoicing, Australia/NZ GST tax-invoice rules, and utility-specific billing are not instantiated.
Exact statutory retention periods (often 6-10 years) remain N1/tax overlays, not enumerated per jurisdiction.
UBL FreightInvoice, DebitNote and Reminder are classified but not given dedicated bundles.
conflicts: UBL Invoice means a request for payment; 19 CFR 141.86 commercial invoice is a customs valuation document and may exist without a payment claim.
Peppol and EN 16931 use date-only YYYY-MM-DD for issue/due/tax point; this model's operational timestamps require RFC 3339 instants with seconds and offset.
A CIUS-only receiver may reject a CORE invoice that uses options restricted out of that CIUS, even though CORE receivers must accept any compliant CIUS.
Credit may be a 381 credit note with positive amounts or a 380 invoice with negative amounts; these are alternative processes, not one canonical encoding.
UBL 2.4 is the current OASIS Standard, while EN 16931 syntax bindings in production commonly still target UBL 2.1 and CII D16B.
Self-billing inverts the UBL submitter role; VAT identity of the supply remains the supplier's.
Proforma invoice (325) shares structure with a commercial invoice but must not be treated as a legally issued payment claim.
regional_assumptions: Default tax-invoice content follows EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC and EN 16931; other VAT/GST regimes need local required-mention overlays.
Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 is treated as the widely deployed European CIUS, not as a global mandate.
US 19 CFR 141.86 is the worked customs-commercial-invoice primary; other customs codes (Union Customs Code, national import invoices) are analogous, not copied.
Public-sector receive-obligation under Directive 2014/55 is European; B2B mandates under ViDA are emerging and jurisdiction-timed.
Modelling assumption (not regional): the seller sequential invoice number is authoritative inside the issuer's series; it is not a global identifier.
Modelling assumption (not regional): issued invoices are immutable commercial objects; corrections use credit notes, corrected invoices or negative-amount invoices according to the chosen process.
Modelling assumption (not regional): date-only legal fields (issue date, due date, tax point) remain calendar dates, while operational observation and ingestion times use RFC 3339 instants.
adversarial_checks: Could this model collapse into N1 Document & Record? No: lines, tax totals, payable amount, type codes and customs valuation are commercial-claim semantics; N1 is referenced for recordkeeping only.
Are payments in scope? Only instructions, prepaid amount and typed settlement links; payment execution is WM-ECO-009.
Is a customs commercial invoice the same object as a Peppol tax invoice? No; legal class and mandatory content differ and are explicit.
Can an issued invoice be patched? Not in this model; successors carry corrections.
Does alignment to UBL imply XML storage? No; UBL is a business-object alignment independent of XML, JSON, PDF, Git, MCP or MongoDB.
